status_detail: No project-level data center facility found in Craven County quick search.
notes: Checked Craven County official economic-development/data pages, industrial properties/history pages, and web/news searches for data center/server farm/colocation/hyperscale. Craven has a Chatsworth Products expansion tied to manufacturing infrastructure for hyperscale/AI/enterprise data-center customers, but I found no Craven County data-center facility project, permit, rezoning, or operator.

project_name: Terra Nexus Ventures Fayetteville Custer Avenue Data Center
status_detail: Local reporting says Terra Nexus Ventures submitted plans to the City of Fayetteville for a data center on Custer Avenue near Eastover and the Fayetteville Public Works Commission power plant. Capacity reporting conflicts: CityView's February 2026 story said 200 MW on 180 acres, while its May 2026 update said 300 MW; recorded 300 MW and flagged conflict.
notes: County page confirms countywide policy review/moratorium context and states the county is not approving a data center through that process. Need Fayetteville planning portal follow-up for original site-plan packet and current status.

project_name: Unnamed PRSM Group client data center
aliases: PRSM Group Cumberland County data center
status_detail: At Cumberland County's May 18, 2026 public hearing on a proposed data-center moratorium, Eric Little of PRSM Group publicly discussed a client's planned 225 MW data center, with closed-loop immersion cooling and estimated 15-18 month construction period. No site address or end user found in quick search.
notes: Included under wide-net policy because the project was presented during an official county public hearing, but the source trail is local news rather than a county staff packet or permit.

status_detail: Energy Storage Solutions floated/planned a 300 MW NetZero data center on Dunn Road in east Fayetteville; local economic-development official Robert Van Geons told CityView in May 2026 that the project is not going to be built. DataCenterMap also lists the Fayetteville NetZero Campus as canceled/archived at 942-1196 Dunn Rd.
notes: Project appears to have been preliminary rather than under contract; kept as rejected/canceled lead because multiple local and tracker sources identify site, developer, and 300 MW concept.

project_name: Advanced Internet Technologies Fayetteville data center
status_detail: CityView reports Fayetteville-based Advanced Internet Technologies, founded in the 1990s, has operated a data center in its headquarters on Hay Street and Maiden Lane.
notes: Small legacy/enterprise hosting facility; no MW found in quick search.

project_name: Plan C Crypto Fayetteville data center
status_detail: CityView reports cryptocurrency mining company Plan C Crypto opened a data center in 2022 in an industrial warehouse on Dedication Drive off Black & Decker Road near Fayetteville Regional Airport and Freedom Christian Academy.
notes: Crypto/digital-infrastructure facility; no MW, permit, or operator page found in quick search.

status_detail: Currituck County official July 30, 2026 news post says no data center projects have been proposed in Currituck County.
notes: County held a July 20, 2026 work session for information gathering; Timmons Group reportedly said no existing or proposed data centers are in eastern North Carolina and that most NC data centers are near Raleigh-Durham and Charlotte. Search found no contrary project-level evidence.

status_detail: No Dare County data-center project found in official site/EDA/planning-style searches or local/news searches.
notes: Searches for Dare County data center/server farm/colocation/hyperscale were dominated by generic vendor SEO pages and unrelated policy/social results. Nearby Currituck official work-session summary also reported no existing or proposed data centers in eastern North Carolina as of February/July 2026.

status_detail: No formal Davidson County data-center proposal found; commissioners discussed/directed drafting of a six-month moratorium before proposals are submitted.
notes: Checked county/news/social searches. Change.org and social posts refer to Lexington/Davidson opposition, but WUNC states officials wanted to create guidelines before any proposals are submitted; Reddit/news snippets likewise say no developer, rezoning request, or proposal in Davidson County.

status_detail: No formal Davie County project found; the county adopted a one-year data-center moratorium on July 7, 2026 after resident concern about potential large industrial/data-center development.
notes: WFAE/WFDD reports unanimous one-year moratorium and public concern over a possible 600-acre industrial campus; OurDavie headline/search snippet says there are not any formal proposals to build a data center in Davie County. Davie Against Data is community/social evidence only.

project_name: Carolina Portway Rose Hill modular data center site
aliases: Rose Hill 1.5 MW modular data center
status_detail: A LinkedIn announcement by Troy Bradshaw says Carolina Portway LLC is launching a 35-acre industrial site in Rose Hill, Duplin County, designed for initial 1.5 MW modular data center capacity with master-plan scalability and fiber connectivity at the boundary. No county permit/EDA announcement found in quick search.
notes: Kept as low-confidence early lead. Duplin County EDC/buildings-and-sites pages were checked, but the identified project evidence is currently a developer LinkedIn post and a matching community Facebook search result, not an official county filing.

status_detail: CyrusOne's official Durham page lists DUR1 in Durham, NC as a data center spanning more than 420,000 square feet in Research Triangle Park. Historical source trail indicates CyrusOne acquired the Sentinel Data Centers NC-1 Durham site in 2017.
notes: Official CyrusOne page confirms operational facility and square footage but not MW. Address commonly listed by directories as 2223 Northeast Creek Parkway, Durham/RTP.

project_name: MCNC Research Triangle Park Data Center
status_detail: MCNC markets secure 24x7x365 data center services, and directory/tracker sources list the Research Triangle Park facility at 3021 E Cornwallis Road in Durham.
notes: Official MCNC pages confirm data-center services and Durham headquarters address; DataCenterMap supplies specific RTP facility listing. No MW found in quick search.

status_detail: TierPoint's official Raleigh-RTP page describes a secure data center in Durham near Raleigh, home to a multitenant cloud pod and part of TierPoint's nationwide data-center network.
notes: Address commonly listed in directories as 99 T W Alexander Drive, Research Triangle Park/Durham. No MW found in official source in quick search.

status_detail: AceHost's official Raleigh-Durham Data Center page lists a 14,000-square-foot facility at 4518 S. Miami Blvd., Durham, NC 27703, with security and power features.
notes: Included as an operating colocation/hosting data-center facility; no MW found in quick search.

status_detail: Energy Storage Solutions proposed a $19.2B multi-phase AI/data-center and energy-storage campus in the Kingsboro development area near Tarboro, with reports varying from 300 MW initial to 900 MW final. DataCenterDynamics reported July 15, 2026 that the developer withdrew the project earlier in July while county officials mulled a 24-month moratorium; DataCenterMap lists the campus as canceled.
notes: Official county site has a June 23, 2026 Data Center Advisory Group report page confirming county policy review context, but the project withdrawal and capacity details are from industry/local reporting and trackers. Capacity recorded as 900 MW final buildout; some reports cite 300 MW initial phase/campus variants.

project_name: Energy Storage Solutions Tarboro Anaconda Road Data Center
status_detail: Energy Storage Solutions applied for a Special Use Permit for a data center and energy-storage project on a 52.185-acre tract near Anaconda Road/McNair Road in Tarboro. Local reporting described 250MW/1000MWh BESS support; WRAL and DCD described an eight-phase 300 MW data center campus. Tarboro Town Council rejected the SUP, and the developer appealed in November 2025.
notes: Kept separate from Kingsboro because sources distinguish the 52-acre Tarboro/Anaconda Road SUP from the larger Kingsboro megasite/campus. Appeal status needs court follow-up.

aliases: Drox Group Rural Hall data center
status_detail: Drox Group proposed a hyperscale data-center campus near Glade Street and Bethania-Rural Hall Road across from Rural Hall Town Hall. Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Planning Board voted 7-2 on June 11, 2026 to recommend denial; local TV reported in early August 2026 that Forsyth County commissioners denied the rezoning request.
notes: Official planning minutes confirm the proposed data center rezoning review, staff/planning-board denial recommendation, utility/water/noise discussion, and that the proposed facility was much bigger than current county data centers. Community site provides project name, parties, 128.54-144 acre range, three two-story buildings, and 1,122,300 sq ft, but those details should be verified against the full rezoning packet.

status_detail: Segra's official colocation page lists a Winston-Salem data center among its owned/operated facilities; DataCenterMap and Datacenters.com list the facility at 3310 Old Lexington Road. MoreThanJustParks tracker reports 6 MW, while official Segra material emphasizes a 120,000-square-foot facility.
notes: Legacy DataChambers facility built/operating in Winston-Salem, acquired by North State in 2011 and then by Segra in 2020. Capacity MW comes from tracker, not official Segra page.
